components.text: Whether the proposed contrast exhausts the available explanatory modes for purposive behavior.
Whether physical-law and personal explanations exhaust the relevant kinds of purposive causal explanation.
Whether simplicity supplies a unitary ordering when descriptive, ontological, and computational measures diverge.
Whether scientific movement toward more complex but better-fitting theories limits the stated simplicity preference.
Whether a single simplicity preference can connect fewer postulates to greater explanatory probability.
Whether familiar personal explanation provides relevant background support for bodiless instantaneous cosmic agency.
Whether the proposed personal explanatory mode is applicable to an unembodied cosmic agent given established causal knowledge.
Whether a simple creator hypothesis supplies discriminating expectations rather than accommodating any observed outcome by an unspecified desire.
Whether verbal brevity can count as explanatory simplicity when it purchases no predictive specificity.
Whether a verbally simple creator hypothesis yields discriminating expectations for observed general features.
Whether verbal economy alone makes a hypothesis explanatorily preferable when it lacks specificity.
Whether an infinite divine agent is simple under the relevant ontological, descriptive, and computational criteria.
Whether qualifications concerning evil and future free actions complicate the proposed divine attributes.
Whether an infinite divine agent is simple under the relevant economy criteria rather than merely verbally concise.
Whether a temporal omniscient God can distinguish a universal present from future free actions under relativity.
Whether the temporal and epistemic divine attributes used to accommodate free agency cohere with physical accounts of time.
Whether grave suffering is justified by agency when many victims are deprived of meaningful agency by suffering or early death.
Whether consequential freedom explains suffering that removes rather than enables a victim's opportunity for moral agency.
Whether evolved functions and algorithms constitute a third causal explanatory category beyond physical and personal explanation.
Whether algorithmic and evolved purposiveness supplies a causal explanatory type beyond physical selection and personal agency.
Whether scientific acceptance of more complex theories defeats simplicity as a probability guide.
Whether simplicity operates only after predictive adequacy and evidential fit are held suitably fixed.

Whether simplicity remains relevant when explanatory fit and predictive accuracy impose additional constraints.
Whether theism meets the response's evidential-fit condition through precise and discriminating predictions.
Whether simplicity often trades against specificity, making a concise hypothesis evidentially weak.
Whether the fit-qualified simplicity rule gives theism sufficiently precise and discriminating predictive content.
Whether broad expectations of order and consciousness are precise enough to support comparative probability.
Whether the proposed account of consciousness coheres with evolutionary history and the explanatory role of the physical brain.
Whether divine production of conscious agents coheres with evolutionary embodiment and the functional cost of large brains.
Whether an independently created soul supplies a coherent mechanism for rational conscious agency.
Whether victims whose earthly lives are gravely bad can receive a victim-centered good sufficient to answer the moral objection.
Whether God can meet obligations toward victims whose earthly suffering or premature death deprives them of a good life.
Whether later compensation can restore the embodied opportunity for moral development lost through premature suffering and death.
Whether a terrible earthly life itself supplies a warrant for the asserted posthumous compensation.
Whether later benefits can compensate for the specific lost opportunity of prematurely killed children to develop moral character.
Whether the freedom rationale applies to victims prevented from developing consequential agency.
